ops.title: ship --tip-only kept a child on an advanced parent's old head by design (#363), not a rewritten-parent bug
ops.body:
Defect report (tooling-ccx-tiponly-moved-parent): `ccx vcs ship --tip-only --no-commit` left a child branch on its parent's old head af3cb8c after the parent moved to 45df523, printing "published <child sha>" each time.

Evidence (monorepo reflog of the parent's remote-tracking ref): af3cb8c -> 45df523 at 15:35 Oct 26 was a fast-forward push of one commit; `git merge-base --is-ancestor af3cb8c 45df523` is true. The rewrite onto a new grandparent was earlier (1be9494 -> af3cb8c at 14:47), and the 14:54 tip-only ship did replay the child onto af3cb8c ("moved <child> onto the published heads").

Mechanism: stackPlan's tip-only branch calls stackTipStays(b, parent published head); OldBase af3cb8c is an ancestor of 45df523, so b.Stays=true and the tip is pushed unchanged. That is the behaviour #363 (07412bc8, Oct 10) chose on purpose: "--tip-only replays nothing: a tip whose parent's published head moved past its base stays on that base", after a tip-only replay onto an advanced parent conflicted. The plan line "stays on <base> · lacks <parent>@<head> · --tip-only keeps a base its parent still holds" only shows in --dry-run; the ship report says just "published <sha>".

So the report's premise (rewritten parent) does not hold, and its expected behaviour reverses #363. Returned to the root as a design fork; no code changed.
